newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia accepts BIS membership - governor.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia accepts BIS membership - governor.

text.p: The governor of Bosnia's central bank said on Friday it had accepted an offer by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) to become a member along with most of the other former Yugoslav republics.
"Bosnia-Hercegovina has also accepted the membership to BIS", the French governor of Bosnia's central bank, Serge Robert, told Reuters.
The Basle-based BIS has invited recently the central banks of Bosnia, Croatia, Macedonia and Slovenia to subscribe to shares in the international organisation of central banks.
Robert said Bosnia would buy 10 shares at $12,294 each offered by the BIS in order to be able to attend the meetings in Basle.
The BIS invitation was an interim solution while the four states and new Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, continue talks on dividing assets of former Yugoslavia's central bank.
